clue.text: All through change of form, trees need time to keep going

indicators.note: a change of a word's form means its letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
firs are evergreen trees
T is the standard abbreviation for time
to last is to keep going, to endure

explanation.surface: A forest changing shape, with trees needing time to keep growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something from beginning to end means covering the whole of it, completely and throughout.

clue.text: Catch what was said of Americans in Britain

indicators.note: a remark that was said is something heard spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: the wartime British gibe called American servicemen overpaid, oversexed and over here

explanation.surface: Picking up the comments made about American troops stationed in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Second World War, Britons complained that the GIs were 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'; the last phrase sounds like OVERHEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark not meant for you is to hear it by accident, eavesdropping without intending to.

clue.text: The Queen's circle's in the Circus

definitions.note: the answer is the statue found in that place

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher
the letter O is round like a circle
the possessive ending contributes its letter

explanation.surface: The Queen's ring of friends appears at a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circus is London's Piccadilly Circus, whose famous winged statue is popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: The aluminium statue at the centre of Piccadilly Circus is universally known by the Greek love god's name.

clue.text: Leading Conservative is briefly among the moderate ones with former date for show from 10 and partner

indicators.note: being among the group means sitting inside it

parts.note: wets were the moderate Conservatives of the Thatcher years
is shortened to its contraction 's
the ides were dates in the old Roman calendar
a prominent Conservative is a Tory

explanation.surface: A political manoeuvre where a Tory squeezes in among the party moderates to fix a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is ROMEO and his partner is Juliet: West Side Story retells Romeo and Juliet in New York. Wets was Mrs Thatcher's dismissive name for moderates in her party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bernstein musical transplants Shakespeare's tragedy of young lovers to rival gangs in Manhattan.

clue.text: Slips are awful things — don't start!

indicators.note: telling the word not to start means its opening letter goes

parts.note: terrors are dreadful, frightening things

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that slips are dreadful, with a plea not to begin on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, so slips are minor mistakes or blunders made carelessly.

clue.text: Franco-German cheese gala taking minimum time

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese; the Franco half applies here
Fest is German for a festival or gala, the German half

explanation.surface: A cross-border celebration of cheese on the French–German frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco-German' splits across the two words: the cheese is French and the gala is in German.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of brief describes whatever lasts the shortest possible span of minutes.

clue.text: Mrs Marcos says she isn't so young

indicators.note: what she says is spoken, so the sound of her words matters

parts.note: someone not so young declares herself older

explanation.surface: The Philippine first lady admitting her age.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, 'I'm elder' matches the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Imelda Marcos was the wife of Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos, famous for her shoe collection.

clue.text: Puzzles with answers running 1 of lines and broad Scots clue I must solve

definitions.text: Puzzles with answers running 1 of lines

indicators.note: solving a problem means working it out, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: The setter faces a clue in broad Scots dialect that he must crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is FROM FIRST TO LAST: in a double acrostic the first and last letters of the lines each spell a word.
explanation.definitionFit: These word puzzles hide answers in both the initial and final letters of a set of lines read downward.

clue.text: Boating clothes in Durham?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what one would wear on the water
second meaning: the waterway that loops round the city of Durham

explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is the river flowing through Durham, a city in north-east England; the question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfits for rowing would be clothing for the water, while the Wear is a real river through Durham city.

clue.text: Lover needs capital as well as love

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: A lover needs money as well as affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero gave his name to any ardent male suitor or womanising admirer.

clue.text: Impressionist goes to poll with drunkard

parts.note: MORI was a well-known British opinion polling company
a sot is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A mimic heads off to vote alongside a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests a comic mimic; it is the painter Berthe Morisot.
explanation.definitionFit: Berthe Morisot was a French painter who exhibited with Monet and Degas in the Impressionist movement.

clue.text: Blue (Conservative) characters bid as little as possible

indicators.note: the words are treated as a set of loose characters, letters to be dealt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Con is the usual abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Tory-blue party members making the most modest offer they can.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative party colour, which makes the bracket look like a gloss rather than more letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the lowest possible opening bid is for a single trick above six in the lowest suit.

clue.text: 'Ave no one perceive one's thought

indicators.note: the dropped aitch of this Cockney spelling tells you to drop an H the same way

parts.note: to hide something is to make sure no one sees it
a means one

explanation.surface: A Cockney insisting that nobody should see what someone is thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have no one perceive' is an instruction to hide; the dropped H of 'Ave shows the H must go from it too.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or concept formed in the mind, the same as a thought.

clue.text: Raptor without wavering asks me to show in 18's clue

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bird goes round

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey

indicators.note: wavering words are unsteady and do not hold their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird of prey steadily asks to be shown something from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 hints at shrews, and Cole Porter's musical is based on The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's musical comedy reworks Shakespeare's Taming of the Shrew, the play alluded to by shrews in 18.

clue.text: This is misplaced among the undoubted: it's just a guess

indicators.note: being among something places it inside that thing

parts.note: sure means certain, beyond doubt
read as 'mis' placed: the first syllable is the piece and the rest tells you it is put somewhere

explanation.surface: Something wrongly filed among the certainties turns out to be mere guesswork.
explanation.walkthrough: Split misplaced as mis-placed: those three letters are placed inside the word for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A surmise is a conjecture made without firm evidence, nothing more than a guess.

clue.text: Puzzler says he is wandering: find them in the fridge

indicators.note: what the setter says is spoken aloud in his own words, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: the setter calls himself I, so he strays becomes I strays

explanation.surface: A crossword setter admits his mind wanders, and something is in the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves as I; put 'he is wandering' (he strays) into his mouth and it becomes the spoken phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice trays are the moulded containers kept in a freezer compartment for making cubes.

clue.text: Curtailment of a nice day shortly before becoming diabolical

indicators.note: said shortly, the day name is cut to its abbreviation

parts.note: a day of the week

indicators.note: curtailing cuts off the tail, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pleasant day cut short and turning thoroughly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Sat is the short form of Saturday; 'shortly before' looks like a time phrase but shortly works on day.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means of or like Satan, the devil, so devilishly wicked and evil.

clue.text: Boys from here came from the 21 of 5, according to copper in Sayers' novel

definitions.text: Boys from here came from the 21 of 5

indicators.note: the metal sits in the rearranged name
novel means new, so the name is given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman in a Dorothy L Sayers detective story describing where some lads came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 of 5 is The Comedy of Errors, whose twin masters Antipholus and servants Dromio come from Syracuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's farce features the Antipholus and Dromio of this Sicilian city, separated from their Ephesian twins.

clue.text: Spooner's domesticated shrews aren't wild horses with labels

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of word pairs

parts.note: domesticated means tame and shrews are nags; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: Tamed shrews are said to be anything but wild horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aren't wild horses' is a second hint at the same phrase, since nags are also horses. A shrew is a nagging woman, as in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Name tags are labels worn or attached to show who someone is or what something belongs to.

clue.text: Theology turning prophet's heart, five times a dozen

parts.note: Th is the abbreviation for theology, as in ThD

indicators.note: turning the word round means reading it the other way

parts.note: a seer is a prophet; the possessive just links
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: A theologian turning over a prophet's innermost feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prophet's heart' looks like the middle letters of a word, but heart is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty, which is also five lots of twelve.

clue.text: Bone, most of which is thin

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for something thin, not an adjective

indicators.note: taking only most of the word leaves off its final letter

parts.note: a rib is a bone
which refers back to the word Bone itself

explanation.surface: A bone that is mostly very slender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which' points back to the first word, so it supplies the word itself minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon is a long narrow strip of fabric, the epitome of something thin and flat.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill keeping me for fun

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was the showman William Cody
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Wild West showman keeping someone around for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment designed to amuse, so it covers fun, humour and laughter.

clue.text: Live doctor's rounds

parts.note: I am means I live, I exist
an MO is a medical officer, an army doctor; the possessive is a link

explanation.surface: A doctor's ward rounds done live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' looks like a doctor's hospital visits but means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds of ammunition are cartridges or shells, and ammo is the informal word for them.

clue.text: Standard party attended by Lily

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
the arum is a kind of lily

explanation.surface: A political party gathering attended by a woman called Lily.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily looks like a guest's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The labarum was Constantine's military banner bearing the Chi-Rho, a standard carried before troops.

clue.text: Counter-tenors in bed with bird?

indicators.note: the singers are placed in the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
alti is the Italian plural of alto, the countertenor's voice

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about male falsetto singers sharing a bed with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' invites the British slang for a girlfriend; it is a real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small European songbird of the tit family with a black cap.

clue.text: A cast beyond the pale?

parts.note: taken as written
a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A throw that goes out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond the pale' usually means unacceptable; here it means even paler than pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means ash-grey and wan, a complexion more deathly than merely pale.

clue.text: See 4
Unable to swallow half psychology — a dig at 6s and 7s

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the front portion
at sixes and sevens means in disorder, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: the first half of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe at muddled psychology that cannot be swallowed whole.
explanation.walkthrough: '6s and 7s' is shorthand for at sixes and sevens, meaning in confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysphagia is the medical term for difficulty swallowing, and the adjective describes a sufferer.
